Let me analyze this conflict.

Register applicant: "Societa Cooperativa Bilanciai Campogalliano a.r.l"
Document applicant: "Soc. Coop. Bilanciai Campogalliano"

Both refer to the same Italian company: Società Cooperativa Bilanciai Campogalliano a.r.l. (a well-known Italian scale/weighing instrument manufacturer).

- "Societa" vs "Soc." — abbreviation drift (accent missing on Società, and abbreviation Soc. Coop. for Societa Cooperativa)
- "Cooperativa" vs "Coop." — abbreviation drift
- Legal suffix drift: "a.r.l" present in register, absent in document

These are clearly abbreviation and legal-suffix drift — same entity. Per the rules: "spelling drift, legal-suffix drift, accent differences = same-entity."

For best_value, the rule says same-entity... which value should the fused record carry? The rules specify best_value for document-noise (register) and different-entity (document), but for same-entity it doesn't explicitly say. However, "Number/year format differences that clearly denote the same certificate = same-entity with the register's canonical form." That hints register canonical form is preferred for same-entity. The register likely holds the fuller, canonical legal name: "Societa Cooperativa Bilanciai Campogalliano a.r.l". The document is a truncated/abbreviated form ("Soc. Coop. Bilanciai Campogalliano" — likely the document continues "a.r.l." but text got truncated). The best fused value would be the fuller register form.

So verdict: same-entity, best_value: "Societa Cooperativa Bilanciai Campogalliano a.r.l".

Why: abbreviation and legal-suffix drift of the same Italian cooperative manufacturer; register form is the fuller canonical name.
